2) We're also evaluating a 24-month term instead of 12 — asking for a small pricing concession given the term and the added cluster. What are the options on contract language for environment isolation and a 24-month committed term?

I've attached a sketch from infra that shows the isolation pattern we're thinking (rh-network-segmentation-sketch.png). Procurement (procurement@radianthealth.com) is on copy for timing.

Appreciate a quick read — can we align this week?

Alex / Laura — thanks for pulling this together. Quick technical read: the isolation pattern in the sketch maps to two logical environments on the same control plane (prod and staging) with strict VPC routing rules and separate KV namespaces. Operational notes: 

- Staging will have its own model pins and rollout policies; we will enforce read-only cache sharing (no write-through to prod).
- We recommend quota enforcement per environment to avoid noisy neighbor issues (suggest 8 GPUs baseline, autoscale to 12 — aligns with Alex's ask).
- Provisioning lead time is ~4 business days once the addendum is executed and network peering details are received.

Questions for procurement: do you require a separate SLA for the staging cluster, or is the standard Private SLA acceptable if we include an isolation addendum? Also need point-of-contact for network engineering to exchange CIDR ranges and peering keys.

I’ve sketched the minimal changes to the SOW (attached as a tracked PDF) — assumes environment add-on pricing line item and a one-time provisioning setup fee.

Cheers,

Alex — following up with pricing options. I ran numbers for the two scenarios you asked about: 12-month renewal + staging add-on vs 24-month committed term + staging add-on. Summary below (high-level):

- 12-month + staging: one-time provisioning $12k, monthly commitment (production + staging baseline): $48k/mo, standard renewal discounts apply.
- 24-month + staging: one-time provisioning $10k, monthly commitment: $42k/mo (5% loyalty + term credit baked in), includes priority queueing for scheduled maintenance windows and a 30% credit threshold for burst usage before overage rates apply.

If you can commit to 24 months we can move the provisioning start date earlier and lock pricing for the term; otherwise we will do the standard 12-month amendment. I can prepare a redline-ready amendment and a DocuSign packet once procurement confirms the desired term.
